strings.name: Drew Houston
strings.summary: Drew Houston co-founded Dropbox with Arash Ferdowsi, building cross-device file synchronization into a cloud collaboration business. He led the company through its IPO, product shifts and two major rounds of layoffs. In 2026 Dropbox announced that he and Ashraf Alkarmi would serve as co-CEOs before a planned move to executive chairman. At review, its company page still lists him as co-CEO. Its products are team achievements, not his independent invention of cloud storage.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026. Distinguishes the effective co-CEO arrangement from the planned transition; graduation year follows MIT. Product capabilities are reported from company announcements, not independently tested.
strings.influence.rationale: Co-founded Dropbox and advanced cross-device file synchronization, influencing cloud collaboration for individuals and businesses.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: MIT bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering and computer science, 2005.
strings.facts.f2.label: Co-founder
strings.facts.f2.value: Founded Dropbox with Arash Ferdowsi in 2007.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Cross-device file synchronization
strings.highlights.h1.text: Built Dropbox with the team to help users synchronize, store and share files.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Expanding knowledge-management products
strings.highlights.h2.text: Led the company’s development of products such as Dash, exploring cross-app search and AI-assisted content processing.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Begins a co-CEO transition
strings.timeline.t1.text: Ashraf Alkarmi becomes co-CEO alongside him; Houston’s later move to executive chairman remains a plan.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Dropbox updates Dash
strings.timeline.t2.text: The announcement introduces video and image search and AI content tools, quoting his explanation of the product direction.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Announces another round of layoffs
strings.timeline.t3.text: Announces a reduction of about 20%, or 528 employees, accepting responsibility for the decision and circumstances behind it.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Announces layoffs and restructuring
strings.timeline.t4.text: Announces cuts of about 16%, or 500 employees, citing slower growth and changing skills needed for the AI transition.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Joins Facebook’s board
strings.timeline.t5.text: The company announces his appointment effective immediately; Facebook later became Meta.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Dropbox begins public trading
strings.timeline.t6.text: Class A shares start trading on Nasdaq as DBX; the offering was priced the previous day.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Co-founds Dropbox
strings.timeline.t7.text: Starts the company with Arash Ferdowsi to address file synchronization and access on the move.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Graduates from MIT
strings.timeline.t8.text: Completes undergraduate studies in electrical engineering and computer science.
